And I understand as well as reconciled that PPOP growth, which is operating profit growth has been 21%, which is again higher, but still lagging the loan growth, which only means that NIMs have a bit compressed.

Advances 27% growth, 3% growth out of this 27% growth is the contribution coming from the IBU, which today has become a sizable book for us, INR8,200 crores in almost 8 to 9 months is what we have built there.
Margins & costs: Operating profit has shown a healthy growth of 2 1% year-on-year with adding INR547 crores, our OP is INR3,117 crores.

Our credit cost has also come down by 20 basis points and has remained within our guidance of maintaining credit cost below 1%.
Capex & expansion: We are the bank which is also differentiated in terms of faster expansion.
They are also required to be making new customer acquisitions in the new geography in the new pin code that where we have opened our branch.
We have also seen that private capex or maybe renewable energy, data centre, all these are emerging new areas, which has also helped lenders, the clean energy, the solar projects.

Last year, against FY22 number of INR600-odd crores of recovery in written -off book, we did INR1,375 crores.
Against a NIM guidance of 3.75% at the beginning of the year, we closed the year with a NIM of 3.91%.
Growth & demand: Total business this year has grown at the rate of 17% and within which advances grew at 22%.
Total deposits grew at 14%, within which our focus, which had always remained on CASA, CASA grew at a double -digit 12%.
The asset side, the RAM had good growth, within which retail was growing at 32%.
Margins & costs: OP, operating profit, INR10,826 crores, grew Y -o-Y at 16%.
We have contained our cost to income below our guidance of 40%, and it closed with 37.08%.

Capex & expansion: And through our quick acquisition, quick disposal, we have even grown our corporate book Y-o-Y at 22%.

With this kind of a geographical expansion, I think no bank in PSB space and particularly the large players who saw amalgamation and mergers, they had to logically go for some sort of a rationalization where some branches had to be closed down.
And sir, the assignment number, right, which gives in the BSE disclosure, that gives like INR14,000 crores is the aggregate amount of loan that we have acquired through assignment.
Balance sheet & cash: With regards to tax, sir, average tax rate is coming around 10% to 11% because we are getting a deduction in the forms of bad debt provision also under 36(1)(viia) & 36(1)(vii) - two sections mainly we are operating where we are getting deduction.
So put together, it is INR1,984 crores, to help to understand -- so around INR2,000 crores of debt waiver amount is what one can expect.
And second, the Board has proposed a dividend, the final dividend amount is around 12% and -- including the interim dividend of 10%.
Risks & challenges: And I'm happy to share that we have seen yet another good year for the bank despite whatever, I should say, challenges, geopolitical uncertainties and a real war for deposit s also.
